reports.title: Leslie Pates
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: Develop a checklist to ensure all members of the Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) have engaged with patients and their family prior to discharge.
promises.summary: Create MDT checklist for discharge communication

promises.quote: To ensure all patients and families have every opportunity to discuss plans and have a dedicated name and contact number for the social worker managing their discharge.
promises.summary: Provide dedicated social worker contact for families

promises.quote: All patients returning home with care package will have their equipment needs assessed and documented in hospital.
promises.summary: Assess equipment needs for home care packages

promises.quote: All plans of care for patients must be shared with the patient and, with patient's consent, their next of kin and agreed before discharge.
promises.summary: Share care plans with patient and next of kin before discharge

promises.quote: A Pilot of "Sick Patients Home Other Plan" (SHOP) is in progress on two medical wards. This is to be escalated across the trust over the next 3 months and become embedded Practice.
promises.summary: Roll out SHOP pilot across trust

reports.title: Elsie Mallalieu
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: Response Following detailed investigations, action has been taken to minimise the risk of inappropriate transfer occurring in the future. Training has been provided to doctors in the Orthopaedic Department to make them aware of the following: (a) That a patient's consultant or alternatively a senior member of the consultant's team must be involved in any decision to transfer a patient between specialties and / or ward areas and that the discussion about transfer and the decision taken must both be clearly
promises.summary: Provide training on appropriate ward transfers and documentation

promises.quote: Page 8 of the Trust's internal investigation report confirms the outcome of the Trust's investigations; that at the time of handover from the Trauma Unit to Ward 41 the need for high-flow oxygen therapy and the skills to use that equipment should have been discussed and resolved before any transfer was completed. The on-call physiotherapist who was familiar with the equipment for high-flow oxygen attended the ward to review Mrs Mallalieu and was available to assist the nursing staff with it.
promises.summary: Train staff on high-flow oxygen equipment use and ensure availability of trained personnel

promises.quote: The Trust's internal investigation identified deficiencies in the record keeping in this case and is undertaking a review of its current training on record keeping standards. Such training will reinforce the need for clarity and completeness.
promises.summary: Review and improve record keeping training standards

promises.quote: staffing levels on Ward 41 did indeed meet the national guidelines. The ward was staffed with auxiliary staff in addition to the two qualified nursing staff. However, since Mrs Mallalieu was treated the Trust have taken further action to reduce the use of agency staff and address substantive vacancies and ensure Registered Nursing levels are maintained. Nurse staffing levels are being monitored through multiple assurance sources including the Trust Board Hard Truths paper. Additionally, the Trust's
promises.summary: Monitor staffing levels and maintain registered nursing staffing ratios

promises.quote: The NEWS system is more sensitive than most other existing systems and it provides an enhanced level of surveillance and clinical review of patients with greater specificity in identifying those at risk of clinical deterioration. In relation to the example given of a doctor who attended on Mrs Mallalieu at 2.30am and "guessed
promises.summary: Implement NEWS system for early detection of patient deterioration

promises.quote: Although, as addressed above, Mrs Mallalieu should not have been transferred to Ward 41 from the Trauma Unit it is certainly not the case that she was "written off'. Nevertheless, admittedly she was a very ill patient with a poor prognosis and this was supported by the Trust's commissioned independent expert report of Consultant [name redacted] which was sent to your offices prior to the inquest.
promises.summary: Clarify escalation decisions and review DNAR documentation
